assertions.description: ProgressEvent is a constructor on Window. This is the baseline the service-worker realm is being aligned with — it is the comparison point, not the feature.
ProgressEvent accepts lengthComputable, loaded and total in its init dictionary and reads them back — the three attributes this feature names.
assertions.test: (() => { const e = new ProgressEvent('progress', { lengthComputable: true, loaded: 512, total: 2048 }); return e.lengthComputable === true && e.loaded === 512 && e.total === 2048; })()

assertions.description: ProgressEvent is constructible inside a DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope. The worker builds one and reports its own result; the page does not infer it.
assertions.test: (async () => { const code = 'try { var e = new ProgressEvent("progress", { lengthComputable: true, loaded: 1, total: 2 }); self.postMessage(typeof ProgressEvent === "function" && e.loaded === 1); } catch (err) { self.postMessage(false); }'; const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([code], { type: 'application/javascript' })); const w = new Worker(url); try { return await new Promise((resolve) => { const t = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 4000); w.onmessage = (ev) => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(ev.data === true); }; w.onerror = () => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(false); }; }); } finally { w.terminate(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url); } })()

assertions.description: THE FEATURE: ProgressEvent is exposed in ServiceWorkerGlobalScope and can be constructed there. A registered service worker constructs one and reports back over MessageChannel; nothing is inferred from the page's own realm.
assertions.test: (async () => { if (!('serviceWorker' in navigator) || !window.isSecureContext) return false; const scope = '/v157/expose-progressevent-in-service-workers/scope-probe/'; const reg = await navigator.serviceWorker.register('/v157/expose-progressevent-in-service-workers/scope-probe/sw.js', { scope }); await navigator.serviceWorker.ready; const worker = reg.active || navigator.serviceWorker.controller; if (!worker) return false; return await new Promise((resolve) => { const channel = new MessageChannel(); const t = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 5000); channel.port1.onmessage = (ev) => { clearTimeout(t); const d = ev.data || {}; resolve(d.exposed === true && d.constructed === true); }; worker.postMessage({ type: 'probe' }, [channel.port2]); }); })()

assertions.description: The values a worker reads off a ProgressEvent are JS numbers carrying fractional precision, per the IDL double type adopted in Chrome 136 — so a relay forwarding platform-constructed values inherits that precision instead of re-deriving it.
assertions.test: (async () => { const code = 'try { var e = new ProgressEvent("progress", { lengthComputable: true, loaded: 1.5, total: 3.5 }); self.postMessage(typeof e.loaded === "number" && e.loaded === 1.5 && e.total === 3.5); } catch (err) { self.postMessage(false); }'; const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([code], { type: 'application/javascript' })); const w = new Worker(url); try { return await new Promise((resolve) => { const t = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 4000); w.onmessage = (ev) => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(ev.data === true); }; w.onerror = () => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(false); }; }); } finally { w.terminate(); URL.revokeObjectURL(url); } })()

assertions.description: lengthComputable defaults to false when the init dictionary omits it — the attribute that lets a relay say honestly that the server sent no content-length, rather than claiming a known total.
assertions.test: (() => { const e = new ProgressEvent('progress'); return e.lengthComputable === false && e.loaded === 0 && e.total === 0; })()
